content: Swine influenza, also known as swine flu, is an illness caused by any virus belonging to the Orthomyxoviridae family that is endemic to pig populations. Viruses that are endemic in swine are referred to as swine influenza viruses (SIV). All identified strains of SIV are classified under Influenzavirus A, which is common, or Influenzavirus C, which is rare. Influenzavirus B has not been observed in swine populations. Among humans, all three clades of influenza viruses—Influenzavirus A, B, and C—are known to be endemic. Swine influenza viruses have the potential to mutate into forms that enable human-to-human transmission. The strain responsible for the 2009 swine flu pandemic is thought to have undergone such a mutation. In humans, the clinical symptoms of swine flu closely resemble those of seasonal influenza or other influenza-like illnesses.
